clue.text: Bill promises to pay after new dog first becomes aggressive

indicators.note: dog first tells us the dog's letters open the whole answer
after says the bill and the promises come behind the letter for new

parts.note: a pug is a small breed of dog
AC, short for account, is a bill
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A bill-dodger's IOUs, delivered after a new puppy arrives, provoke someone into turning hostile.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are read in a different order from the clue: 'dog first' puts PUG at the front, then N, then AC + IOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pugnacious is a straightforward synonym for combative, eager to pick a fight.

clue.text: Classy naval NCO's husband

parts.note: a PO, petty officer, is a naval non-commissioned officer; with the possessive S that gives POS

explanation.surface: A petty officer's husband is described as rather upmarket.
explanation.definitionFit: Posh is the informal British word for upper-class or smart.

clue.text: Yellow ducks, for example, seen around marsh

indicators.note: the game birds are seen around the marsh, so its letters sit inside

parts.note: ducks are game birds, hunted for sport
a bog is a marsh

explanation.surface: Yellow-billed ducks are spotted on a marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamboge is a deep yellow pigment from a tree resin, and the colour named after it.

clue.text: Contact — a whimsical-sounding one touring north

indicators.note: sounding says the words 'a quaint' are taken as spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: quaint means oddly whimsical, so 'a whimsical' is 'a quaint', said aloud like the verb acquaint

indicators.note: the ace goes round the letter for north, enclosing it

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: Someone you keep in touch with is described as charmingly odd while travelling up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounding' works on 'a whimsical', read as 'a quaint'; 'touring' has the one go round north, giving the ending.
explanation.definitionFit: A contact is someone you know, and an acquaintance is just such a person.

clue.text: Woman identifies with first murder victim

parts.note: 'is' links a thing to what it is identified as, as in 'he is the boss'
in Genesis Abel, killed by Cain, is the first murder victim

explanation.surface: A woman sees herself in the Bible's first murder victim.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabel is a female first name, so it is an example of a woman.

clue.text: High-class writer with tailless dog, standing erect

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class usage
a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: tailless means the dog loses its last letter

parts.note: a dingo is an Australian wild dog

explanation.surface: A posh author with a dog that has lost its tail stands up straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Upending something sets it on end, so it is a way of standing an object upright.

clue.text: Missile Soviets introduced — something to chew over?

indicators.note: introduced puts the Soviets' letter at the start, introducing what follows

parts.note: S is short for Soviet, as in USSR
cud is what cows chew over again

explanation.surface: A Soviet missile appears, giving everyone something to ponder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something to chew over' looks like a thought to consider, but it is the cud a cow chews.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scud is a Soviet-designed short-range ballistic missile, so the name stands for one.

clue.text: Acknowledge record formerly held by English

indicators.note: held by puts the word for formerly inside the record

parts.note: a CD is a compact disc, a record
once means formerly

explanation.surface: An admission that the English used to hold a certain record.
explanation.definitionFit: To concede a point is to admit or grant that it is true.

clue.text: With the current duke, have new master

parts.note: to own is to have

indicators.note: new signals the letters of master in a fresh order

explanation.surface: The present duke takes on a new master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the current duke' reads as the present holder of the title, but 'With the current' is the definition, a current in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Something carried along with the flow of a river is moving downstream.

clue.text: Bridge players tremble receiving intelligence agency's note

indicators.note: receiving means the intelligence agency's letters are taken inside

parts.note: S and E, South and East, are partners at bridge
to quaver is to tremble
MI, Military Intelligence, as in MI5 and MI6

explanation.surface: Card players tremble on receiving a message from the secret service.
explanation.definitionFit: A semiquaver is a musical note, a sixteenth note, half a quaver.

clue.text: Precipitation beginning to settle at present

indicators.note: beginning to takes only the opening letter of settle

parts.note: now means at present

explanation.surface: Falling flakes are starting to lie on the ground at this moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow is one form of precipitation, along with rain and hail.

clue.text: Weakness in a country novel the Spanish girl finally digested

indicators.note: digested means the country takes the girl's last letter inside it

parts.note: Chile is a South American country

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of girl

parts.note: She is a novel by H. Rider Haggard
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A girl from Spain devours a novel about a foreign country, exposing her weakness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like an anagram signal, but it stands for the novel She by H. Rider Haggard.
explanation.definitionFit: An Achilles heel is a vulnerable spot, named after the hero's one unprotected point.

clue.text: Noble widow's party bet, mostly payable before game

indicators.note: before puts the earlier pieces ahead of the game

parts.note: a do is a party
a wager is a bet

indicators.note: mostly drops the last letter of the word for payable

parts.note: due means owed, payable
chess is a board game

explanation.surface: An aristocratic widow's party has a bet, largely due before a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager duchess is the widow of a duke, keeping the title after his death.

clue.text: Shield university kept in battered chest once

indicators.note: kept in means the university letter is held within the reworked letters
battered signals the letters of chest once knocked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A university once kept something in a battered old chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battered' rearranges CHEST ONCE into ESCTCHEON, and U goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An escutcheon is a shield bearing a coat of arms, in heraldry.

clue.text: Novelist bringing Worthing's alter ego way to the front?

indicators.note: the word for way is moved to the front of the alter ego's name

parts.note: in Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest, Jack Worthing goes by Ernest in town
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: An author brings Jack Worthing's town persona to the fore.
explanation.walkthrough: ERNEST with ST moved from its end to the front gives STERNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne was an 18th-century novelist, author of Tristram Shandy.

clue.text: Eg Brunel's technique ultimately, never without spirit

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of technique
without here means outside, so the word for never goes around the spirit

parts.note: ne'er is the poetic contraction of never
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A tribute to Brunel's methods, which never lacked spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Isambard Kingdom Brunel was a famous Victorian civil engineer, so he is an example.

clue.text: Revealing falsehood suppressed by one of the Archers?

indicators.note: in a down answer the falsehood is held down, placed below the archer

parts.note: William Tell is the legendary archer
a tale is a lie, a falsehood

explanation.surface: A lie is hushed up by a character in the radio soap The Archers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap, but here the archer is William Tell.
explanation.definitionFit: A telltale sign is one that gives something away, so it is revealing.

clue.text: Impartial peacekeepers stationed around India

parts.note: the UN sends peacekeeping forces

indicators.note: around means the word for stationed goes around the letter for India

parts.note: based means stationed
I is India in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Neutral peacekeepers are deployed around India.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbiased means without prejudice, the same as impartial.

clue.text: Officer's servant engaging old person in row, perhaps?

indicators.note: engaging means taking in, so old's letter goes inside

parts.note: a batman is an army officer's personal servant

explanation.surface: An officer's servant takes on an elderly person in an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel, but it is rowing a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rows or hires out boats is a boatman, the 'perhaps' marking an example.

clue.text: A better article in French about S American mammal

indicators.note: about turns the whole string around to read backwards

parts.note: to cap something is to better it
la is a French definite article

explanation.surface: A superior French article about a South American animal.
explanation.walkthrough: A + CAP + LA gives ACAPLA, which read backwards is ALPACA.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpaca is a domesticated South American camelid kept for its wool.

clue.text: Enduring a heartless injunction

indicators.note: heartless removes one of the middle letters of the word for injunction

parts.note: a bidding is a command, an injunction

explanation.surface: A lasting order lacking compassion.
explanation.definitionFit: Abiding means lasting or permanent, a synonym of enduring.

clue.text: Help tidy up school appeal?

parts.note: a co-ed is a co-educational school
it means sex appeal

explanation.surface: A school appeal asks for help tidying the place up.
explanation.definitionFit: To coedit a text is to share in editing it, helping to polish it.

clue.text: Keeping register back, risks joint state office

indicators.note: keeping means the risks hold the reversed register inside

parts.note: chances are risks

indicators.note: back means the register is read in reverse

parts.note: a roll is a register, a list of names
the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: Holding on to a register at the back puts a joint state agency in danger.
explanation.definitionFit: The chancellorship is the office of chancellor, a high government post.

clue.text: Meet round rear of Garrick for burlesque

indicators.note: the word for meet goes round the picked letter

parts.note: a committee sits, or meets

indicators.note: rear of takes the final letter of Garrick

explanation.surface: People gather around the back of the Garrick for a send-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The Garrick is a London theatre and club, named after the actor David Garrick.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit is a short comic parody, a kind of burlesque.

clue.text: TV award this writer rejected? Goodness!

indicators.note: rejected means the word for the writer is turned back

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as this writer, giving me
my! is an exclamation like goodness!

explanation.surface: A writer is snubbed for a television prize, to their astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The Emmy is the main American television industry award.

clue.text: Tufted material originally clicked with Shetland, town right away

indicators.note: originally picks the opening letter of clicked

parts.note: and means with

indicators.note: right away removes R, the abbreviation for right

parts.note: Lerwick is the main town of Shetland

explanation.surface: A tufted fabric first caught on in a Shetland town.
explanation.definitionFit: Candlewick is a soft cotton fabric with raised tufted patterns, used for bedspreads.

clue.text: Not any composition left unfinished!

indicators.note: unfinished cuts off the final letter of the composition

parts.note: a nonet is a musical composition for nine players

explanation.surface: No composition is left unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: None means not one, not any at all.

clue.text: Touch down on river following try-out of plane

indicators.note: on means the word for touch down comes after

parts.note: the Test is a river in Hampshire
to light is to alight, to land

explanation.surface: An aircraft lands by a river after a trial run.
explanation.definitionFit: A test flight is a trial flight to check how an aircraft performs.
